title: Serve-fidelity credits: measurable SLA definitions, error budget formula and escalation steps for Dedicated
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Purpose: define a compact, measurable SLA and error-budget/crediting mechanism for Redwood Dedicated customers that balances predictable economics with operational realities. This ticket codifies metric definitions, the error-budget math, measurement windows, exclusions, and a default remediation/escalation ladder for contract language and engineering work.

Scope: definitions for measurable contract terms (what we guarantee and how we measure it), a deterministic credit formula for shortfalls, the schedule for customer notifications and credit issuance, required dashboards/monitors, and sample contract snippets for legal review. Does NOT include bespoke negotiated addenda; those will be derived from this canonical model.

Key outputs: canonical metric names and formulas, one-page credit computation examples, an escalation/playbook for incident -> credit, monitoring instrumentation checklist, and proposed consumer-facing contract paragraph(s).
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff with Eng infra and Observability. Agreed to measure at the per-customer reserved pool level rather than per-VM.
2026-03-04: Product/Legal alignment session — legal prefers a single simple credit formula with caps rather than tiered subjective remediation language.
2026-03-06: Eng proposed telemetry schema for GSR and burst windows; added ENG-74821 as dependency to export new metrics to billing pipeline.
2026-03-09: Drafted credit calculation examples and shared with Billing and Sales for feedback. Sales requested clearer language for 'force majeure' and scheduled maintenance windows.
2026-03-10: Design review scheduled; started preparing sample contract paragraph for legal review (see attachments).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical metric definitions documented and implemented in telemetry (GSR, CapacityUtil, DegradationEvents)
Deterministic credit formula with worked examples signed off by Product, Billing and Legal
Monitoring dashboard with SLO burn and automated alert for predicted credit trigger
Contract paragraph(s) and remediation ladder drafted for legal review
deliverables: SLA glossary + measurement guide (GSR, measurement windows, exclusions)
Error budget and credit computation worksheet with 3 examples (minor, moderate, severe)
Escalation & remediation playbook for Customer Success and Support
Draft contract paragraph and sample amendment language for Legal
open_questions: Should we express the commitment as tokens-per-minute or as request-rps equivalency for mixed workloads?
If autoscaler fails to add capacity for a customer-initiated spike, do we count that as a service shortfall or as an excluded operationally-triggered modal?
Do credits apply only to monthly committed fees or also to overage/consumption line items?
Should we provide a hard cap on cumulative service credit in a rolling 12 month period?
How to treat cross-AZ failovers where only one AZ degrades but global throughput remains within commitment?
monitoring_metrics: GuaranteedServeRate (GSR) — measured as 1-minute rolling tokens served per reserved-minute, aggregated per customer pool
CapacityUtilization — median and 95th percentile utilization of reserved GPU pools tied to customer entitlement
DegradationEvent — boolean flag when measured GSR falls below threshold for > 5 consecutive minutes
AutoscaleFailCount — number of autoscale decisions where desired capacity increase failed due to infra constraints
measurement_windows: Primary window: 30-day rolling measurement to determine eligibility for credits. Short-term detection: 5-minute and 1-hour windows drive alerts and initial mitigation. Long-term aggregation for contractual crediting uses calendar-month alignment unless customer requests otherwise.
example_credit_calculation: Formula: MonthlyServiceCredit = min(CreditCap, Floor(CommittedFee * ((CommittedGSR - ObservedGSR) / CommittedGSR) * WeightingFactor)) where WeightingFactor = 30 for converting 1-minute shortfalls to monthly proportion. CreditCap = 0.5 * CommittedFee by default. Example: customer committed 600M tokens/month for $30,000. ObservedGSR averaged 90% of committed over the billing month -> shortfall ratio=0.10 -> credit = min(0.5*30k, 30k * 0.10) = $3,000. If shortfall is severe (observed 50% of committed) credit = min(15k, 30k * 0.50)=15k. Adjustments: exclude scheduled maintenance windows and documented 3rd-party infra outages; prorate for partial-month changes to entitlement.
escalation_flow: 1) Auto-detect: Observability raises DegradationEvent and pages on-call with customer context. 2) Triage (within 30 mins): SRE confirms measurement fidelity and attempts immediate mitigations (hotfix routing, temporary overprovisioning). 3) Mitigation window (up to 4 hours): engineering executes remediation playbook; Customer Success notified. 4) If remediation fails within 4 hours, Product issues a 'service-impact' notification to customer and logs an Incident. 5) Post-incident (48–72 hours): measurement reconciliation and calculation of MonthlyServiceCredit if the 30-day aggregated shortfall passes threshold. 6) Credit issuance: apply as billing credit within next invoice cycle and provide a root-cause and remediation summary to customer. Appeals allowed within 30 days with supporting telemetry.
legal_snippet_suggestion: Sample clause: 'Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide Dedicated Serve Capacity at or above the Guaranteed Serve Rate (GSR) defined in the Order. If Redwood fails to meet the committed GSR for a given billing period, Customer will be eligible to receive a Service Credit calculated in accordance with the parties' credit computation worksheet. Service Credits are Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for any failure to meet the GSR, subject to exclusions for scheduled maintenance, Customer-caused overprovisioning, and force majeure.'
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Measurement noise leading to spurious credits. Mitigation: implement smoothing, anomaly filtering and manual reconciliation guardrails.
Risk: High operational overhead from appeals. Mitigation: provide transparent raw telemetry and automated reconciliations to reduce friction.
Risk: Perverse incentives for customers to trigger credits during controlled experiments. Mitigation: require advance notice for permanent entitlement changes and exclude known test windows.
